setup.title: Messenger
setup.intro: Set up how your Messenger chat greets and guides customers — the Get Started button, a welcome greeting, an always-on menu, and tappable FAQs. Pick a feature, read what it does, then fill it in. Changes save straight to Facebook.
setup.loadError: The Messenger profile could not be loaded. Try again.
setup.failed: That did not work. Try again.
setup.footnote: These settings write to the Facebook Messenger profile via the Graph API and apply to new conversations. Meta may take a moment to propagate changes.

getstarted.title: Get Started button
getstarted.subtitle: The button a brand-new customer taps to begin the chat.
getstarted.what: It is the very first thing someone sees when they open your Messenger — a single “Get Started” button on the welcome screen.
getstarted.customer: They tap it once, and the conversation begins. It only ever shows before the first message.
getstarted.how: Give it a payload (a keyword like GET_STARTED). Then in Flows, add a Trigger that listens for that payload so a Welcome flow runs the moment they tap.
getstarted.payloadHint: This word is sent to you when the button is tapped. Match it in a Flow trigger to start automation.

greeting.title: Greeting
greeting.subtitle: The friendly welcome line shown before anyone types.
greeting.what: A short welcome message on the very first screen of your chat, right under your Page name.
greeting.customer: They read it the instant they open your Messenger — it sets the tone and tells them what you can help with.
greeting.how: Keep it to one warm line (max 160 characters). Tip: add a first-name tag and Messenger greets each customer by name.
greeting.placeholder: Hi there! How can we help you today?
greeting.sample: Hi! How can we help you today?

menu.title: Persistent menu
menu.subtitle: The always-on shortcut menu inside the message bar.
menu.what: A menu (the ☰ icon next to the text box) that stays available all through the chat — up to 3 shortcuts.
menu.customer: They tap ☰ at any point to jump straight to what they need — “Talk to a human”, “Track my order”, “Visit shop”.
menu.how: Add up to 3 items. Each one either runs a Flow (send a payload) or opens a link (URL). Optionally hide the text box so people only use the menu.

ice.title: Ice breakers
ice.subtitle: Suggested questions shown before the first message.
ice.what: Up to 4 tappable questions on the welcome screen — the common things people ask, ready to tap instead of type.
ice.customer: Instead of thinking what to write, they tap a question like “What are your hours?” and get an instant answer.
ice.how: Add your top FAQs. Each tap sends its payload — match that payload in a Flow trigger to answer automatically.

help1.title: What can I post?
help1.body: Photos, albums, links, feed videos and reels publish straight to your connected Page through the Graph API.

help2.title: How does scheduling work?
help2.body: Pick a time between 10 minutes and 75 days out and Facebook queues it — it publishes automatically when due. Or publish now.

help3.title: A post failed — why?
help3.body: Usually the media URL was not public HTTPS, or the Page was reconnected. Read the error on the row, then retry with Publish now.
